findings.issue: Message: «отображаемое имя содержит недопустимые символы — уберите спецсимволы (<, &, #, кавычки, скобки) и попробуйте снова». Judge live-verified this exact character list against the real KC person-name-prohibited-characters validator (t-0633-keycloak-1): <, &, #, ", ( all independently reproduced a 400 with this validator's messageKey; apostrophe (') and hyphen (-) — NOT named in the message — both independently verified to PASS (KC accepts them), so the message does not over-claim. Human, jargon-free, names the actual problem field, gives a concrete example of what to remove, ends with an actionable next step («попробуйте снова»). No dev/internal terms ("KC", "person-name", "validator", error codes) leak into the visible string.
findings.suggestion: None required — flagged only to record the live character-list verification for the record, not because anything is wrong.

findings.issue: When BOTH email and display_name are invalid in the same submit (KC's {errors:[...]} multi-field shape, live-confirmed), the fix surfaces only the name problem first (AP-9 case 3) — the owner fixes the name, resubmits, and only then discovers the (separately genuine) bad email as a second round trip. Not misleading (the name message is entirely honest and true), just not maximally complete in one pass. Consistent with this form's existing single-error-per-response model (EMAIL_TAKEN/LOGIN_TAKEN are likewise one code per response, never aggregated) — not a new deviation introduced by this task.
findings.suggestion: Non-blocking. Acceptable as-is given the existing single-field-error convention across this entire form; aggregating multiple field errors into one response would be a broader form-wide redesign out of scope for a NF-1 attribution fix.
